newsitem.title: USA: BankBoston brightens on Venezuela, Philippines.
newsitem.headline: BankBoston brightens on Venezuela, Philippines.

text.p: BankBoston Corp said on Monday it increased its portfolio weightings for the Brady bonds and debt instruments of Venezuela and improved its credit trend outlook for the Philippines from stable to positive.
Revamped economic policy and enhanced foreign debt-servicing ability prompted BankBoston to up Venezuela from neutral to overweight, BankBoston said.

"We are impressed by results of the IMF-sponsored stabilization program, the likelihood of external debt buybacks next year and the possibility of a credit rating upgrade in 1997," said Peter Allen, managing director and head of emerging markets research at BankBoston.
Although the Philippines appears to be a candidate for a ratings upgrade in first-half 1997, BankBoston maintained its underweight recommendation for the country, Allen said.
"We maintain our underweight portfolio recommendation for Philippine foreign debt instruments due to the relatively tight spreads and low yields available on these instruments," he said.
The future of privatizations, public-sector restructuring, labor law improvement and social security reforms will be key to the investment quality of Philippine debt, Allen said.
